summary: A report from the Internet Architecture Board on the role of the Internet Research Task Force (IRTF), on its own and in relation to the IETF. It grew out of IAB discussion while a new IRTF chair was being appointed. It is informational.

eli5.summary: The Internet has a group that builds things and a group that does long-term research. This note is a board explaining what the research group is for and how it fits with the builders.

subtitle: The Internet Architecture Board's perspective on the role of long-term Internet research.

tldr.problem: The Internet community has long-term research needs distinct from short-to-medium-term engineering. There is ambiguity about what role the Internet Research Task Force (IRTF) should play relative to the IETF's standards work, and how research and development communities should interact.
tldr.mechanism: The IAB clarifies that the IRTF is a forum for investigation of areas not yet ready for standardization, with research groups that do not need to achieve consensus. Research group output can inform IETF standards but has no special weight in the standards process. The RFC outlines the range of group structures and discusses how the IRTF can bridge research and development communities.
tldr.outcome: The document establishes the IRTF's role as complementary to the IETF's but distinct: non-blocking, not consensus-driven, and focused on longer-term issues. However, gaps remain in how to best leverage the IRTF for architectural work and how to improve interchange between research and standards communities.

today: RFC 4440 is an Informational RFC published in March 2006 documenting the IAB's perspective on the IRTF's role. It has not been obsoleted or updated. The IRTF continues to operate under RFC 2014 as amended, with the strategic vision outlined in this RFC informing discussions about the IRTF's evolution and relationship to the broader Internet community.

sections.title: The IRTF and the IETF
sections.content:
In 1989, the Internet Activities Board reorganized two major groups: the IETF (Internet Engineering Task Force) took on short- to medium-term engineering and standards work, while the IRTF (Internet Research Task Force) took on long-term research. The IAB (now Internet Architecture Board) oversees both.

The key difference is that the IETF produces Internet standards through consensus-based working groups, while the IRTF conducts research without requiring consensus. IRTF research groups investigate areas not mature enough for standardization or that fall outside the scope of standards altogether. When an IRTF group produces a proposal suitable for standardization, it goes through the same standards process as any other proposal and receives no special weight.

Early in Internet history, the IETF had strong participation from academic and research institutions. Over time, as the Internet matured and commercialized, the IETF became dominated by industry needs, while the IRTF maintained stronger ties to academia and research communities.
sections.eli5: The IETF builds standards for things the Internet needs soon. The IRTF explores bigger questions about where the Internet should go long-term. They are separate because the IETF has to ship, and the IRTF has to think.

sections.title: How IRTF Groups Differ from IETF Working Groups
sections.content:
IRTF research groups have two fundamental differences from IETF working groups. First, IRTF groups are not trying to produce standards of any kind. Their output is research results, which may or may not lead to standards later. Second, consensus is not required within an IRTF group; research groups can publish minority views and exploratory work without needing agreement from all participants.

A research group also acts as a non-blocking entity: it does not gate or prevent work elsewhere. Existing research groups do not prevent new research groups in related areas, and IRTF activity does not block IETF standardization. This flexibility lets IRTF groups serve as a breeding ground for ideas without the constraints that consensus-building imposes.

In practice, IRTF groups span a wide range. Some are open to all; others are closed or invitation-only. Some are long-term, ongoing communities; others are short-term with specific deliverables. Some focus on feeding ideas to the IETF (like the Crypto Forum Research Group), while others pursue independent research with no planned IETF connection (like the Delay-Tolerant Networking Research Group).
sections.eli5: IRTF groups explore ideas without needing everyone to agree. They do not have to produce standards, and they do not block anyone else's work. That freedom lets them take risks and follow interesting questions that the IETF might not have time for.

sections.title: The IRTF's Role in Architecture and Research-Development Relations
sections.content:
The IAB identifies a major opportunity: the IRTF should help with questions of network architecture. The spectrum of potential work ranges from visionary (where are we, and where should we go?) to specific problem-solving. Some IRTF groups have tackled broad architectural questions successfully (the End-to-End and Routing Research Groups), while others focus on studying a specific proposal in depth.

Another key role is bridging research and development communities. As the Internet has matured, research participation in the IETF has declined, and disconnections between researchers and operators have emerged. For instance, significant work on QoS (Quality of Service) lacked input from operators on real deployment challenges. The IRTF can serve as a forum where researchers and IETF technologists work together, improving communication in both directions.

To strengthen the IRTF-IETF relationship, the IAB suggests clearer communication pathways: IETF working groups should inform the IRTF of research problems that need investigation, and IRTF groups should present findings to the IETF. Some IRTF groups might adopt a design-team-like relationship to IETF working groups, with chartered deliverables and timelines. However, this must be voluntary: IRTF groups depend on volunteers' interest, so forced relationships do not work.
sections.eli5: The IRTF can explore big architectural questions that the IETF does not have time for, and help researchers and industry technologists understand each other better. The IETF can tell the IRTF what hard problems they face, and the IRTF can explore them carefully without the time pressure of shipping standards.

sections.title: Status and Open Questions
sections.content:
RFC 4440 is an Informational RFC published in March 2006. It documents IAB thinking on the IRTF's evolving role but does not mandate specific changes. The document identifies several open questions for future discussion: how to better use the IRTF for architectural work, whether research group names should change (some view "Research Group" as off-putting), how to improve the RFC publishing track for IRTF output to distinguish it from IETF standards, and how to improve dialogue between research and standards communities.

The RFC reflects uncertainty about how the IRTF will evolve, with the IAB suggesting that evolution should be explored collaboratively over time with the IRTF Chair and leadership. The document explicitly notes that the IRTF should not become a de facto dumping ground for technologies that are not making progress in IETF working groups; rather, technologies should move to the IRTF only when open research questions exist that justify investigation.
sections.eli5: This note is the IAB saying: 'The IRTF has been helpful, but we think it could be even better. Here are some ideas for how.' It leaves many questions open for the IRTF Chair and leaders to work out over time.

items.text: Develop and evaluate emerging approaches before they are ready for standardization.

items.text: Focus on well-defined problems where many pieces exist but key challenges remain unsolved.
